run.question:
The checkout-service in production-us-east-2 is throwing 500 errors right
now. Investigate the root cause using app-269-prod-logs.

report.summary: The production-us-east-2 checkout failures are logged, and the log text itself names the mechanism: payment-service's charge calls to the external provider stripe-us timed out after 30 s, and checkout-service then failed /api/checkout on the payment-provider timeout and afterwards on an open circuit breaker for payment-service (failure rate 41%). Observed rows in app-269-prod-logs for cluster production-us-east-2 in the authorized window: 08:19:41Z payment-service ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'; 08:19:41Z checkout-service ERROR 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)'; 09:19:41Z checkout-service ERROR 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)'; 09:49:41Z checkout-service ERROR 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open' (the newest error row in the window). The logs show 'POST /api/checkout failed' at ERROR level; the numeric HTTP 500 is not itself printed in these rows. Rows with the same timestamps but cluster production-eu-west-2 ('Healthy: p95 latency 220ms' for checkout-service, 'Adyen-eu healthy' for payment-service) are a different cluster and do not clear production-us-east-2. The only Kubernetes cluster readable in this Run is production-eu-west-2; its app-269 checkout-service is a different entity (nginx:1.27-alpine, scaled 0->1 by its own Deployment at 10:19:38Z, fresh pod ready with 0 restarts and only nginx startup logs) and is not the failing service named in the question. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable on every attempt (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no metric, alert-state or span evidence exists in this Run; the affected cluster's workloads could not be inspected at object level, and the state of stripe-us itself is unknown. The conclusion rests on the exact log messages plus the cluster field of those documents, in the app-269-prod-logs index on the registered source (its only index).

claims.text: The registered log source contains exactly one index, app-269-prod-logs (6 documents), with keyword fields cluster, level, service and message and date field timestamp; its documents carry cluster values production-us-east-2 and production-eu-west-2, so it does hold data for the cluster named in the question.
cluster=production-us-east-2, service=checkout-service logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-22T08:19:41Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)'.
cluster=production-us-east-2, service=payment-service logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-22T08:19:41Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'.
cluster=production-us-east-2, service=checkout-service logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-22T09:19:41Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)'.

cluster=production-us-east-2, service=checkout-service logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-22T09:49:41Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open'; this is the newest row in app-269-prod-logs inside the authorized window.

The rows in the same index at the same timestamps but with cluster=production-eu-west-2 (checkout-service INFO 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms' at 08:19:41Z, payment-service INFO 'Adyen-eu healthy' at 09:49:41Z) describe different entities in a different cluster and therefore do not show production-us-east-2 health.

In the only readable cluster (production-eu-west-2) a separately named Deployment checkout-service exists in namespace app-269 with image nginx:1.27-alpine; its own Deployment event 'Scaled up replica set checkout-service-6d7f474c45 from 0 to 1' is at 2026-11-22T10:19:38Z, its new pod checkout-service-6d7f474c45-sdcd8 is Running and ready with 0 restarts (startTime 10:19:38Z), and its container logs contain only nginx startup lines.

That the production-eu-west-2 app-269 checkout-service pod created at 10:19:38Z caused or is part of the production-us-east-2 checkout errors: it is a different cluster and a different workload (nginx:1.27-alpine), its creation comes from its own Deployment/ReplicaSet as Normal events, its pod has 0 restarts and only nginx startup logs, and the production-us-east-2 errors began about two hours earlier at 08:19:41Z.

That an active fault-injection flag on the payment path explains the production-us-east-2 errors: in the readable production-eu-west-2 cluster's otel-demo namespace, ConfigMap flagd-config holds paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable') with defaultVariant 'off' for both, and that ConfigMap belongs to a different cluster and namespace than the production-us-east-2 payment-service.

The only checkout-related alerting rule readable (ConfigMap prometheus in otel-demo, production-eu-west-2) is CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh over traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"} with rule label cluster="opspilot-m1"; it targets the otel-demo namespace, not the production-us-east-2 checkout-service named in the question, and its firing state could not be read because Prometheus was unreachable.

The origin is one hop deeper than payment-service, at the external payment provider stripe-us, whose /v1/charges calls took longer than 30 s; no available source exposes stripe-us state, so this remains unverified and it is not established whether the provider itself, the network path or payment-service's own 30 s timeout configuration is responsible.

Advise checking stripe-us charge-endpoint availability and latency for 2026-11-22 08:19Z onward and reviewing payment-service's 30 s upstream timeout and the checkout-service circuit-breaker thresholds (41% failure rate observed) before resetting the breaker; once Prometheus is reachable, confirm with traces_span_metrics_calls_total status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count for service_name=payment-service and checkout.

gaps: No metric evidence: every Prometheus call in this Run returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (get_metric_names, get_label_values, get_prometheus_target, get_metric_metadata path, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, list_prometheus_rules), so checkout error ratio, span error status, latency series and alert firing state for production-us-east-2 are unknown, not zero.

No trace evidence: traces_list_services and traces_search both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level call edge between checkout-service and payment-service and no span status/latency was observed.

Kubernetes access covers only production-eu-west-2; the production-us-east-2 checkout-service and payment-service Deployments/Pods, their replicas, restarts, events, and the ConfigMaps that configure the 30 s timeout and circuit breaker could not be read, and their namespace is unknown.
The external payment provider stripe-us has no data source in this Run; whether it was failing, slow, or unreachable is unverified.
No change history integration is available, so no configuration change or deployment for production-us-east-2 can be identified or timed.

Whether the circuit breaker was still open at the end of the window is unknown: the newest matching error is 09:49:41Z and the index holds only 6 documents in total, so log completeness/retention cannot be assessed.
The numeric HTTP 500 status is not printed in the matching log rows (they read 'POST /api/checkout failed'), so the exact status code comes from the question, not from observed log content.
next_steps: Confirm stripe-us (payment provider) charge endpoint status and latency for 2026-11-22 08:19Z onward.
Once Prometheus is reachable, query production cluster metrics for checkout-service '.*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' error ratio and payment-service upstream duration/error series.
Inspect production-us-east-2 checkout-service and payment-service workload configuration (30 s upstream timeout, circuit-breaker thresholds) and recent changes to them.

data.alertmanager.yml:
global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] /etc/alertmanager/opspilot/token
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] ${env:PROMETHEUS_COLLECTOR_PASSWORD}
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
